concept.title: How the pressure washer works
concept.shortdesc: The takes water from a standard garden hose and uses a pump to raise its pressure to as much as . The spray gun and nozzle turn that pressure into a focused stream that removes dirt, mildew and loose paint.

section.title: The path water takes
section.p: Water enters the pump through the garden hose inlet. A screen in the inlet catches debris that could damage the pump. The electric motorgasoline engine drives the pump, which pushes the water through the high-pressure hose to the spray gun. The nozzle on the end of the spray wand narrows the stream and sets the spray pattern.

section.title: What happens when you release the trigger
section.p: When you release the trigger, water has nowhere to go. An unloader valve senses the rise in pressure and sends the water back through the pump in a loop. This is called bypass mode. On the electric model, the motor also shuts off automatically after a few seconds in bypass mode and restarts when you squeeze the trigger again.On the gas model, the engine keeps running in bypass mode.

Water that loops in bypass mode heats up. A thermal relief valve releases hot water from the pump before it can damage the seals. If you see water dripping from under the pump after a long pause, the valve is working as designed.

section.title: Choosing a nozzle
section.p: A narrower spray angle delivers more force to a smaller area. Start with the widest nozzle that does the job, and move to a narrower one only if needed.
